title: The roadmap gets re-weighed as a whole, and notes stay short
why: Your question, Oct 26: are we rewriting notes instead of appending, and re-weighing the order instead of putting each new item at the front? Audit, Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045: mostly not.
note: Audit, Oct 26 at roadmap 9517045 (full text: project files reports/roadmap-upkeep-audit.md): 85 of 135 note edits were appends; 15 of 84 notes passed 300 words; no existing step was ever re-ordered; all 14 steps filed since Oct 25 landed in the top 12, the last four at ranks 1 to 4; the whole-roadmap review never ran, because its trigger (a phase change) never fired. Your ruling, Oct 26 ('agreed, let's implement this'): this thread, 'Triage the roadmap', is the gatekeeper. Only it creates, merges, orders and closes steps; other threads send it each item with your message attached and still rewrite notes on their own steps. The coordinator wrote the rule into the project instructions. Built Oct 26: build.py prints an upkeep list on each build (notes over 250 words; in phases with an active step, steps untouched 5 days and empty notes; new top-5 steps with no 'Placed ahead of' line). Done Oct 26: long notes on c23, c27, c44, c48, c49, c54, o8 and o13 rewritten; cleanup order re-weighed to the build advisor's batch order. Open: c51, c52 and c53 notes, owned by the build advisor; a whole review of the design, rollout and later phases (21 steps untouched since Oct 17 to 21, 11 with no note), at the next batch merge. Placed ahead of c53 (triage, Oct 26): it governs how every later step is filed, and it builds nothing in claude-settings main.
